data.body:
Epic handoff. 3 of 15 children closed and merged (F1, F12, F13). 6 in progress on a Gerrit stack (2530/2531/2533/2535/2536/2537), every one LLM-Review +1 and Verified -1 — reviews passed, CI is red on two unconfirmed causes: a `require resolvable rebar ticket` failure on 2530 that does not reproduce locally, and a ~50s pytest failure that looks like a collection/import error and also does not reproduce locally. 6 open, of which F8 (certified, unclaimed) is the cheapest next piece and F11 is deliberately blocked behind the bc66 module split.

Scope grew by one child during execution: eagleeyed-commutable-mantisray (bc66) splits src/rebar/_cli/_registry.py at its validation seam. It exists because _registry.py sits at EXACTLY the 800-line cap and F11 must edit it. Splitting a module inside a mirror-remediation change would have put an unrelated refactor in a change whose reviewed plan is about single-sourcing a policy set. Four other src/rebar files also sit at exactly 800, so this hazard is general; the ticket records them.

AC2 of this epic — no fix collapses a distinct concept — did real work rather than being decorative. Three fixes were narrowed or reshaped by it: F3 left composer._TYPES alone because the full create vocabulary is a different concept with its own ticket (F7); F4's no-relist check matches PROPER subsets so it does not flag CANONICAL_RELATIONS, which belongs to F8; and F5 baselined 41 pre-existing model gaps against their own ticket rather than changing the published MCP outputSchema inside a gate refactor.

Three findings were also filed outside this epic: cyclopean-bloodshot-hoatzin (root-disk outage, owned elsewhere), tomophobic-ambient-killdeer (the plan-review deterministic floor is not deterministic), and lowly-lawrencium-ovenbird (the 41 MCP schema gaps).
